{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_5fed4369d5d5477090357bd4","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Deliver a user's conversation list over the WebSocket protocol\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#144\n4\tLabels: type:feature, size:M, area:api, area:compliance, epic:extension-points\n5\t\n6\tPart of #35\n7\t\n8\t## Why\n9\t\n10\t#143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)`.\n11\tIt does not give a **client** anything: the browser holding the socket cannot reach the store, so\n12\tevery consumer that wants a history sidebar has to stand up its own authenticated HTTP route over\n13\tthe same data the engine already authenticated on the upgrade. That is a second authorisation\n14\tpath to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership\n15\tcheck wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.\n16\t\n17\tA consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session\n18\tstore and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already\n19\treplays a conversation on resume; answering \"which conversations do I have\" over the same socket\n20\tis the smaller surface.\n21\t\n22\t## What to do\n23\t\n24\t- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:\n25\t  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into\n26\t    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the\n27\t    connection's authenticated user's.\n28\t  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`\n29\t    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as\n30\t    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types\n31\t    describe what goes on the wire.\n32\t- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;\n33\t  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as\n34\t  the two existing cases do it.\n35\t- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the\n36\t  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the\n37\t  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a\n38\t  streaming answer.\n39\t- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:\n40\t  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own\n41\t  list.\n42\t- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through\n43\t  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an\n44\t  `error` frame and no list.\n45\t- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client\n46\t  that renders \"no conversations\" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that\n47\t  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.\n48\t- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which\n49\t  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second\n50\t  replay path.\n51\t- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their\n52\t  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list\n53\t  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`\n54\t  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and\n55\t  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.\n56\t\n57\t## Decisions\n58\t\n59\t- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is\n60\t  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.\n61\t- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it\n62\t  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not\n63\t  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.\n64\t- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). A list request\n65\t  that queued behind a two-minute streaming answer would look broken, and it mutates nothing.\n66\t- **An error, not an empty list, when it cannot be answered.** See above; silence that looks like\n67\t  data is the one failure mode a history view cannot recover from.\n68\t- **Answered when asked, never pushed.** No `conversation_list` arrives unsolicited: a client\n69\t  that just started a conversation knows, and a push would need a fan-out across the sockets a\n70\t  resumed session can be open on.\n71\t- **The frame is accepted by `validateMessage` whether or not the feature is on**, and the\n72\t  handler is what refuses it. That is a second authorisation\npath to the same personal data, written once per consumer, each one able to get the ownership\ncheck wrong in its own way — the exact failure #45 went out of its way to avoid for resume.\n\nA consumer may have no such route to extend: an engine deployment behind an api with a session\nstore and no conversation endpoints of its own has nothing to add this to. The engine already knows who is connected and already\nreplays a conversation on resume; answering \"which conversations do I have\" over the same socket\nis the smaller surface.\n\n## What to do\n\n- `src/types/messages.ts`, additive only:\n  - `ListConversationsMessage {type: 'list_conversations'; limit?: number; before?: string}` into\n    `IncomingMessage`. There is no user id field, and that is the point: the list is always the\n    connection's authenticated user's.\n  - `ConversationListMessage {type: 'conversation_list'; conversations: ConversationSummary[]}`\n    into `OutgoingMessage`, where `ConversationSummary` is `SessionSummary` with its two times as\n    ISO strings — `Date` does not survive `JSON.stringify` as a `Date`, and the protocol types\n    describe what goes on the wire.\n- `validation.ts`: a `list_conversations` case — `limit`, when present, an integer 1–200;\n  `before`, when present, a string `Date.parse` accepts. Anything else is `INVALID_MESSAGE`, as\n  the two existing cases do it.\n- Handling: `createMessageHandler` takes the session store and the new options alongside the\n  orchestrator (`createServer` already holds both), and answers `list_conversations` on the\n  non-locked path beside `ping` — a history request is not a turn and must not queue behind a\n  streaming answer.\n- The user id comes from `ws.userId`, never from the frame. Add the regression:\n  a frame carrying an extra `userId` of another user is answered with the connecting user's own\n  list.\n- Opt-in: `HalEngineConfig.transport.history?: {enabled: boolean}`, default off, threaded through\n  `createServer`'s options like `resume`. With it off, `list_conversations` is answered with an\n  `error` frame and no list.\n- A store that implements no `listFor` is answered with an `error`, not an empty list: a client\n  that renders \"no conversations\" for a user who has several is a worse answer than one that\n  renders a failure. `ErrorCodes` gains one code for both cases (`UNSUPPORTED`), additive.\n- Picking a conversation needs nothing new: the client reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`, which\n  #45 already ships with the ownership check and the replay. No in-band switch frame, no second\n  replay path.\n- Specs and docs: extend `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` (the two frames, their\n  field tables, the authorisation rule) and the conversation-list spec; add § Conversation list\n  to `docs/getting-started.md` by editing `example/full-config.ts` and running `npm run docs:fix`\n  — that listing sits under `<!-- doc-block: example/full-config.ts#full-config -->` and\n  `npm run docs:check` fails a hand-edited block.\n\n## Decisions\n\n- **A frame, not a REST route.** The REST chat routes are demo-only and are not where a consumer is meant to build. The WebSocket is where the caller is\n  already authenticated, once per connection, by the consumer's own `wsAuth`.\n- **Its own opt-in flag, separate from `resume`.** Resume hands a client back a conversation it\n  was already in; a list tells it what else the user has. A deployer who turned on resume did not\n  thereby agree to the second disclosure, and a config that conflates them cannot be audited.\n- **Answered off the per-session lock.** `PerSessionLock` serialises turns (#47). A list request\n  that queued behind a two-minute streaming answer would look broken, and it mutates nothing.\n- **An error, not an empty list, when it cannot be answered.** See above; silence that looks like\n  data is the one failure mode a history view cannot recover from.\n- **Answered when asked, never pushed.** No `conversation_list` arrives unsolicited: a client\n  that just started a conversation knows, and a push would need a fan-out across the sockets a\n  resumed session can be open on.\n- **The frame is accepted by `validateMessage` whether or not the feature is on**, and the\n  handler is what refuses it. Validation is static and has no config; the alternative is\n  threading options into a pure validator to turn a type into \"unknown\".\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `src/types/messages.ts` gains only new interfaces and their two union members (**amended:** four interfaces, not two — each frame needs a type for its own payload, `ConversationCursor` for what a client sends back and `ConversationSummary` for a row on the wire) — a\n      `git diff` of that file touches no existing line, and a fixture pins that every message\n      literal valid before this change still compiles\n- [ ] `validateMessage({type: 'list_conversations'})` is valid; with `limit: 0`, `limit: 201`,\n      `limit: 1.5`, `limit: '10'` or `before: 'not a date'` it is invalid with a message naming\n      the field\n- [ ] With `history: {enabled: true}` and a store holding three conversations for the user, a\n      `list_conversations` frame is answered with exactly one `conversation_list` carrying three\n      summaries, newest first, each `createdAt` and `updatedAt` an ISO string, and no\n      `stream_end`\n- [ ] A frame carrying `{type: 'list_conversations', userId: '<another user>'}` is answered with\n      the connecting user's own list, and the store's `listFor` is called with `ws.userId` —\n      asserted on the recorded argument, not only on the frame\n- [ ] `limit` and `before` reach `listFor` as the frame sent them. **Amended:** `before` is a\n      `{updatedAt, sessionId}` cursor of ISO strings, not a `Date`. This was written before\n      #143's review found that paging on a timestamp alone drops a conversation whenever two\n      share an activity time, so the store's cursor became a composite that accepts an ISO\n      string; a `Date` cannot carry the tie-break. The handler passes `{limit, before}` with\n      both possibly `undefined` rather than omitting the argument, which is the same call\n- [ ] With `history` absent, the same frame is answered with one `error` frame whose code is\n      `UNSUPPORTED` and no `conversation_list`\n- [ ] With `history: {enabled: true}` against a store implementing no `listFor`, the answer is\n      the same `error` frame, and `grep` shows no code path that sends `conversations: []`\n- [ ] A `listFor` that rejects is answered with one `error` frame whose code is `SERVER_ERROR`\n      and whose message carries no store detail, the socket stays open, and the failure is\n      logged with the session id and no user content. **Added during the build:** a store throwing\n      the new exported `StoreCannotList` is answered `UNSUPPORTED` instead, so an injected\n      collection without a `find` reads as the misconfiguration it is rather than a database\n      that failed\n- [ ] A `list_conversations` sent while a `user_message` is streaming on the same session is\n      answered before that turn's `stream_end` — it does not wait on the lock\n- [ ] A client that takes an id from a `conversation_list` and reconnects with `?sessionId=<id>`\n      receives `resumed: true` and that conversation's replay, with no new transport code: the\n      test exercises the existing #45 path end to end\n- [ ] `ConnectedMessage` is unchanged by this issue\n- [ ] **GDPR.** The protocol spec states that `conversation_list` carries one authenticated\n      user's own conversation metadata and no conversation content, that the user id is taken\n      from the connection and never from the frame, and that `transport.history` is the\n      deployer's decision to make a user's history reachable from the client; `SessionResumeOptions`'\n      retention note is mirrored on the new options type, pointing at #41\n- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` carries an entry under `## [Unreleased]` written for somebody installing the\n      package\n- [ ] The `docs/getting-started.md` change is made in `example/full-config.ts` and the doc\n      regenerated with `npm run docs:fix`, not typed into the markdown\n- [ ] Spec statements carry trailing `([validated by: ...](...#Lnn))` citations, `Status` rows\n      match coverage, and `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and\n      `npm run spec:names` pass\n- [ ] The version bump is MINOR — new optional config, two additive protocol frames, one new\n      error code — and the PR body says so; no migration guide is owed\n- [ ] `npm run verify` passes and the coverage floors for the touched groups hold or rise\n\n## Amendments\n\nThree things changed between writing this issue and building it, each marked in the criterion it\naffects:\n\n1. **`before` is a cursor, not a timestamp.** #143's review found that paging on `updatedAt` alone\n   silently drops a conversation when two share an activity time. The store's cursor became\n   `{updatedAt, sessionId}`, so the frame carries both halves and the validator refuses one half\n   alone. Built as originally written, the transport would have reintroduced the defect the store\n   had just been fixed for.\n2. **`messages.ts` gains four interfaces, not two** — the two frames plus the two payload types\n   they describe.\n3. **`StoreCannotList` is new public surface**, beyond what this issue specified: without it a\n   permanent store misconfiguration cannot be told from a transient failure, in either the client\n   frame or the log.\n\nTwo decisions the criteria did not anticipate:\n\n- **`transport.history` without `transport.resume` is useless, and now says so.** `?sessionId=` is\n  read only when resume is enabled, so a list whose rows cannot be opened is a deployment slip:\n  the engine warns at startup and the documentation says so where it tells a client to reconnect\n  with a row's id. Refusing to start was considered and rejected as too blunt for a library.\n- **The conversation the connection is in is listed like any other**, so a fresh connect sees a row\n  of its own holding no entries. Filtering it out was rejected: it is a real conversation the user\n  is in, and it is their newest the moment they send anything.\n\n## Tech notes\n\nDepends on #143: without `listFor` there is\nnothing to send.\n\nKey paths: `src/types/messages.ts`, `src/types/session.ts` (`ErrorCodes`),\n`src/transport/ws/{validation,messageHandler,sender}.ts`, `src/transport/createServer.ts`,\n`src/config.ts`, `example/full-config.ts`, `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: a preview or title on the summaries (its own issue); deleting a conversation from\nthe client, which would put an erasure primitive on the wire and needs its own authorisation\ndecision; paging state held server-side — the client pages with `before`; an operator view of\nanother user's conversations, which is an authorisation question of its own; and live sync between open tabs,\nwhich #124 ruled out.\n\nRefs #143, #145, #41, #45, #47, #124\n\n\n\n\n","numLines":174,"startLine":1,"totalLines":174}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_5fed4369d5d5477090357bd4","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_d49be0bee1384918bba52022","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Definition of Done\n2\t\n3\t> #143 gives a consumer `store.listFor(userId)` inside the server process. The client on the other end of the WebSocket has no way to ask for it, and the consumer who wants a conversation picker without standing up their own REST endpoint has to write one anyway.\n4\t\n5\t**Strategy: `direct`** — `createServer` and the WebSocket upgrade/message pipeline already exist and accept frames over a real WebSocket connection, so acceptance tests can connect today, send `list_sessions` frames, and fail directly on the missing `session_list` and `list_sessions` validation/dispatch behaviour.\n6\t\n7\t## Done when these pass\n8\t\n9\t- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId** — Sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit, before, userId}` over a connected WebSocket and verifies `store.listFor` is called with the socket's authenticated `userId` (`session.userId`) and `{limit, before}`, answering `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings.\n10\t  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n11\t\n12\t- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws** — Verifies that a store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}` and a store whose `listFor` throws/rejects logs an error under category `'ws'` with the userId and error message and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}`.\n13\t  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n14\t\n15\t- [ ] **listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol › accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor** — Verifies that `{type: 'list_sessions'}` is accepted while non-integer or negative `limit` values and malformed `before` cursors (`sessionId` outside 1–128 chars or unparseable `updatedAt`) are rejected with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without invoking `store.listFor`.\n16\t  `src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts`\n17\t\n18\t## Facets\n19\t\n20\t- [x] Add `ListSessionsMessage`, `SessionSummaryFrame`, and `SessionListMessage` to `src/types/messages.ts`, include them in `IncomingMessage` and `OutgoingMessage`, and re-export them from `src/index.ts`.\n21\t- [x] Validate `list_sessions` frames in `src/transport/ws/validation.ts` (optional non-negative integer `limit`; optional `before` object with 1–128 char `sessionId` and finite-date `updatedAt` string or number; strip unknown fields like `userId`).\n22\t- [ ] Thread `sessionStore` into `createMessageHandler` (optional parameter so existing 1-arg and 2-arg callers keep working) and wire it in `src/transport/createServer.ts`.\n23\t- [ ] Handle `list_sessions` in `src/transport/ws/messageHandler.ts` (and helper in `src/transport/ws/sender.ts` if needed) by reading `session.userId`, calling `await sessionStore?.listFor?.(session.userId, {limit, before})`, serialising `Date` fields to ISO strings, and on error logging via `log.error('ws', ...)` and sending `ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR`.\n24\t- [ ] Document `list_sessions` and `session_list` in `specs/hal-engine-websocket-protocol/spec.md` and `specs/hal-engine-conversation-list/spec.md`.\n25\t- [ ] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` written for somebody installing the {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/bdfb6d0de730/home-2/.claude/skills/tdd-loop\n\nThis is the authoritative copy of Lore's TDD contract for agent runs. It is checked\ninto the Lore repo at `apps/mcp-server/agent-skills/skills/tdd-loop/` and served to\npods by the gateway's `/skills` registry.\n\nYou run the three phases yourself, in order, in one pass. Do not skip a phase and do\nnot run two facets in one round.\n\n## The three laws\n\n1. Do not write production code unless it is to make a failing test pass.\n2. Do not write more of a unit test than is sufficient to fail — a compile or import\n   failure counts.\n3. Do not write more production code than is sufficient to make the currently failing\n   test pass.\n\n## Phase 1 — RED\n\nDetect the toolchain from the project (`package.json`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`,\n`Cargo.toml`, `pom.xml`, `Gemfile`, `mix.exs`, `Makefile`, CI config) and mirror the\nconventions already in the repo's tests — framework, directory, file suffix, assertion\nstyle. Assume nothing about the language.\n\n**The one-facet rule.** Name the single smallest behaviour that moves you forward. If\nthe behaviour you were handed would force more than one new facet, write the test for\nthe smallest facet only and report the leftovers rather than growing the round.\n\nWrite **exactly one** test. Run it. Confirm it fails **for the reason you expect** —\nthe behaviour is absent, not the import path typo'd or a fixture missing. A test you\ndid not run is not a red bar, it is a guess.\n\nIf a behaviour would not change the code under test at all, say so and write nothing.\nA test that forces no change is not worth writing.\n\n### No mocks, no stubs\n\nDesign every test to exercise pure logic with real values — value in, value out, not\ninteractions. A facet that seems to *require* a double is a design signal: the real\nproblem is an unmanaged side effect, not the absence of a mock. Pick a facet that is\ntestable without doubles, and note that the production code should push the I/O to the\nedges so the pure core is directly testable.\n\n- Stubbed lookup → pure function on a value. `discountFor(user)` taking a real `User`,\n  not `discountFor(userId)` fetching one behind a `UserRepository` stub.\n- Interaction mock → assert on a returned value. Have the core return the intent and\n  assert `notificationsFor(order)`; sending happens at the edge.\n- Clock/RNG stub → inject the value. `isExpired(deadline, now)`, both plain values.\n\nA true collaborator boundary that must eventually be pinned down is a separate\n**contract test**, never an ad-hoc mock sprinkled into a unit test.\n\n### Test naming\n\nThe principle is language-agnostic; the surface form follows the language.\n\n- Short, clear, scannable. The name carries the expected behaviour **and** the tested\n  data — never the implementation.\n- No \"should\".\n- Apply the *ask-why* check: a name that does not answer why the test exists is a\n  structural name, not an intent-revealing one.\n- Include the context only when the enclosing suite does not already establish it.\n\nGood: `returns 0 for an empty list`, `returns I for 1`, `throws RangeError for 0`.\nBad: `should return zero`, `test sum`, `works correctly`.\n\n## Phase 2 — GREEN\n\nWrite the fewest lines that turn the bar green. No extra features, no speculative\ngenerality, no refactoring yet.\n\n**Kent Beck's green-bar strategies:**\n\n- *Obvious implementation* — when the real code is trivial and unmistakable, write it.\n- *Fake it* — when it is not, return a constant and let a later test replace constants\n  with variables.\n- *Triangulate* — leave generalization to the NEXT test. Do not guess the general\n  solution now.\n\nRun the tests you are working against — the one you just wrote plus the acceptance\ntests that define done — by naming their files. Never the repository's whole suite:\nCI runs that on every push, and the pod's Bash hook refuses a bare `npm test` or\n`vitest run` with no path. All of what you run must pass.\n\n**Never edit the test to make it pass.** If the test is wrong, say so and stop; that is\na finding, not a green bar.\n\n### Where code goes\n\nNever create code in catch-all `utils` / `misc` / `helpers` / `common` / `shared` /\n`lib` modules. Place and name code by the domain concept it serves — discount logic in\n`pricing/`, not `utils/calc.ts`. When no home exists, create a domain-named module,\nnever a generic bucket.\n\n### Naming\n\nMeaningful but concise — one to three words (`pendingOrders`, `isContainer`,\n`retryCount`). No single letters except trivial loop indices; no `temp`/`data`/`x`; no\nsprawling four-plus-word names. Name by role: `rawInput`, `normalized`.\n\n## Phase 3 — REFACTOR\n\nThe bar is green. Improve the design without changing behaviour, and fit the new code\ninto the surrounding architecture. The suite stays green throughout.\n\n**Duplication is duplicated knowledge, not just duplicated text.** Hunt for and\ncollapse: the same business rule expressed two ways, a constant or validation\nre-derived in two places, parallel structures encoding one concept, a domain concept\nnamed differently across modules, the same idea living in both code and a test.\n\nRefactor **both** production and test code. Test refactoring counts: collapsing\nduplicated tests into one parameterized test, removing now-subsumed tests, extracting\nshared setup, clarifying names. Behaviour coverage must not shrink.\n\n### The Simple Design Dynamo\n\nReuse is a **result** of removing duplication, never a prediction. Never extract because\nsomething \"might\" be reused. For each candidate, in order:\n\n1. Remove the duplication — collapse the copies into one. The reusable shape only\n   becomes visible after the duplication is gone.\n2. Separate what varies from what stays the same.\n3. Extract a template — the algorithm steps with explicit variation points.\n4. Name each operation concretely. **If a step cannot be named, the variation is not\n   understood yet — stop and look.**\n5. Parameterize the details — lift literals into arguments. Generic logic in code,\n   specific values in data passed in.\n\nThis loops: removing duplication creates structures → you name them → better names\nraise cohesion → higher cohesion makes the next, bigger duplication visible.\n\n**Rule of three.** Two copies = notice, and remove the duplication *in place*. Promote\nto a shared module only on the third genuinely similar case. Lifting on the second copy\ncouples unrelated callers and is harder to undo than the duplication was.\n\n### Reveal intent\n\nFor any name you touch, ask \"why does this exist / what is it really?\" — the name must\nanswer that, not describe the mechanism. A function name containing \"and\"\n(`parseAndStore`) is two responsibilities; split it. Improve names iteratively:\nnonsense → structurally accurate → intent-revealing.\n\n### Fewest elements\n\nInline indirection that does not pull its weight — a wrapper that only forwards. Apply\n\"too simple to break\": never add a test for trivial composition of already-trusted\nparts. Reject premature abstraction.\n\n### Refactor discipline — this is where rounds go wrong\n\n- **Never change production code and test code in the same step.** Each step touches\n  only tests or only production code, then run the suite to green before the next.\n  Changing both at once means a green bar no longer proves the refactor was safe.\n- One target per step, always.\n- **If a step turns the suite red, revert that step** rather than chasing the failure.\n- Grep for existing abstractions to reuse before inventing new ones.\n- May move or extract code and create files, but never add behaviour or expand scope\n  beyond the current test.\n\n### Out-of-scope smells\n\nWhile you have the context loaded, note architecture and code smells you spot that are\n**unrelated** to the current round — god objects, leaky abstractions, missing seams,\ndead code. **Do not fix them**; that blows the round's scope. Collect them as\n`future_improvements`: location + smell + one-line suggested fix. Report them; act on\nnone.\n\n## Ending the round\n\nCommit and push per the delivery contract in your task instructions — in a pod, the\nwork dies with the container otherwise. Commit only on green; a red suite is never\npushed.\n\nReport: the facet you closed, the facet you would take next, the post-refactor test\nresult, and the `future_improvements` list.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f773dd4f-97e5-4bea-b135-1a2d9a59db99","uuid":"efbf723a-caba-4af2-b26d-817d5f47b6e1","timestamp":"2026-11-04T00:37:07.679Z","isSynthetic":true}

state.suppressOutput = true;\n}\n\nfunction processStopChunk(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, parser: ThinkingTagParser): void {\n  flushHeldText(ws, session, state, parser);\n session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, parser: ThinkingTagParser): void {\n  for (const segment of parser.flush()) {\n    handleTextSegment(ws, session, state, segment);\n  }\n}\n\n// The flag lives on the stored entry even when suppressed; only a visible entry is re-sent, which is how a live client learns it.\nfunction closeCutOff(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState, key: StateIndexKey): void {\n  const index = state[key];\n  if (index === null) return;\n  markTruncated(session, index);\n  if (!state.suppressOutput) sendUpsert(ws, index, session.entries[index]);\n  commitAndClear(ws, session, state, key);\n}\n\nfunction commitOpenEntries(ws: WebSocket, session: ChatSession, state: StreamState): void {\n  commitAndClear(ws, session, state, 'thinkingIndex');\n  commitAndClear(ws, session, state, 'assistantIndex');\n}\n\nfunction handlePing(ws: WebSocket, timestamp: number): void {\n  ws.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'pong', timestamp}));\n}\n","numLines":336,"startLine":1,"totalLines":336}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_6436824f5c8b4a918cb7a88f","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, 't']);\n61\t  clients.push(client);\n62\t  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n63\t  let connected: Frame = {type: ''};\n64\t  await new type {AddressInfo} from 'node:net';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport type {Express} from 'express';\nimport {createServer} from './createServer.js';\nimport {HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL} from './ws/subprotocol.js';\nimport {answeringOrchestrator} from './wsTestSupport.js';\nimport {InMemorySessionStore} from '../infrastructure/stores/inMemorySessionStore.js';\nimport type {SessionCursor, SessionListOptions, SessionStore, SessionSummary} from '../types/sessionStore.js';\nimport {setLogger} from '../shared/logger.js';\n\n// Real upgrades over a real socket: what the list_sessions frame answers is the contract, and no double can observe it.\n\ninterface Frame {\n  type: string;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  sessions?: Array<{sessionId: string; createdAt: string; updatedAt: string; entryCount: number}>;\n  code?: string;\n  message?: string;\n}\n\nconst servers: Array<ReturnType<typeof createServer>> = [];\nconst clients: WebSocket[] = [];\nconst logLines: Array<{level: string; category: string; message: string; fields?: Record<string, unknown>}> = [];\n\nconst eventually = async (check: () => boolean): Promise<void> => {\n  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 50 && !check(); attempt++) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));\n};\n\nbeforeEach(() => {\n  logLines.length = 0;\n  const record = (level: string) => (category: string, message: string, fields?: Record<string, unknown>) =>\n    void logLines.push({level, category, message, fields});\n  setLogger({debug: record('debug'), info: record('info'), warn: record('warn'), error: record('error')});\n});\n\nafterEach(async () => {\n  for (const client of clients.splice(0)) client.terminate();\n  for (const hal of servers.splice(0)) {\n    const {wss} = hal;\n    await eventually(() => wss.clients.size === 0);\n    await hal.stop();\n  }\n  setLogger();\n});\n\nconst startEngine = async (store: SessionStore, userId: string | number = 'u1') => {\n  const hal = createServer({\n    app: (() => undefined) as unknown as Express,\n    wsAuth: async () => ({id: userId}),\n    sessionStore: store,\n    orchestrator: answeringOrchestrator,\n  });\n  await hal.start(0);\n  servers.push(hal);\n  const {port} = hal.server.address() as AddressInfo;\n  return `ws://127.0.0.1:${port}/hal/ws`;\n};\n\nconst askAfterConnect = async (url: string, outbound: unknown): Promise<{connected: Frame; frames: Frame[]}> => {\n  const client = new WebSocket(url, [HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL, 't']);\n  clients.push(client);\n  const frames: Frame[] = [];\n  let connected: Frame = {type: ''};\n  await new Promise<void>(resolve => {\n    client.on('message', raw => {\n      const frame = JSON.parse(String(raw)) as Frame;\n      if (frame.type === 'connected') {\n        connected = frame;\n        client.send(typeof outbound === 'string' ? outbound : JSON.stringify(outbound));\n        client.send(JSON.stringify({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1}));\n        return;\n      }\n      if (frame.type === 'pong') {\n        resolve();\n        return;\n      }\n      frames.push(frame);\n    });\n  });\n  return {connected, frames};\n};\n\n// A store with only the five required members, so listFor can be omitted, recorded or made to throw.\nconst delegatingTo = (inner: InMemorySessionStore): SessionStore => ({\n  create: (sessionId, userId, options) => inner.create(sessionId, userId, options),\n  get: sessionId => inner.get(sessionId),\n  delete: sessionId => inner.delete(sessionId),\n  count: () => inner.count(),\n  clear: () => inner.clear(),\n});\n\ndescribe('listing conversations over the WebSocket protocol', () => {\n  it('answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const seen: Array<{userId: string | number; options?: SessionListOptions}> = [];\n    const summaries: SessionSummary[] = [\n      {\n        sessionId: 's2',\n        createdAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'),\n        updatedAt: new Date('2026-01-01T00:02:00.000Z'),\n        entryCount: 4,\n      },\n    ];\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingTo(inner),\n      listFor: (userId, options) => {\n        seen.push({userId, options});\n        return summaries;\n      },\n    };\n    const url = await startEngine(store, 'u1');\n    const before: SessionCursor = {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:05:00.000Z', sessionId: 's3'};\n\n    const {frames} = await askAfterConnect(url, {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 10, before, userId: 'u2'});\n\n    expect({seen, frames}).toEqual({\n      seen: [{userId: 'u1', options: {limit: 10, before}}],\n      frames: [\n        {\n          type: 'session_list',\n          sessions: [\n            {\n              sessionId: 's2',\n              createdAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',\n              updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:02:00.000Z',\n              entryCount: 4,\n            },\n          ],\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    const withoutList = await startEngine(delegatingTo(inner));\n    const failingList = await startEngine({\n      ...delegatingTo(inner),\n      listFor: () => Promise.reject(new Error('database offline')),\n    });\n\n    const unimplemented = await askAfterConnect(withoutList, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n    const failed = await askAfterConnect(failingList, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n\n    expect({\n      unimplemented: unimplemented.frames,\n      failed: failed.frames.map(frame => ({type: frame.type, code: frame.code})),\n      logged: logLines.filter(line => line.level === 'error' && line.category === 'ws'),\n    }).toEqual({\n      unimplemented: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      failed: [{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}],\n      logged: [\n        {\n          level: 'error',\n          category: 'ws',\n          message: expect.any(String),\n          fields: expect.objectContaining({userId: 'u1', error: 'database offline'}),\n        },\n      ],\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor', async () => {\n    const inner = new InMemorySessionStore();\n    let calls = 0;\n    const store: SessionStore = {\n      ...delegatingTo(inner),\n      listFor: () => {\n        calls += 1;\n        return [];\n      },\n    };\n    const url = await startEngine(store);\n    const badFrames = [\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 'ten'},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: -1},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', limit: 1.5},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: 'not-an-object'},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', sessionId: ''}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', sessionId: 'a'.repeat(129)}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: 'not-a-date', sessionId: 's1'}},\n      {type: 'list_sessions', before: {updatedAt: true, sessionId: 's1'}},\n    ];\n\n    const codes: Array<string | undefined> = [];\n    for (const bad of badFrames) {\n      const {frames} = await askAfterConnect(url, bad);\n      codes.push(frames[0]?.code);\n    }\n    const {frames: accepted} = await askAfterConnect(url, {type: 'list_sessions'});\n\n    expect({codes, accepted, calls}).toEqual({\n      codes: Array(badFrames.length).fill('INVALID_MESSAGE'),\n      accepted: [{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}],\n      calls: 1,\n    });\n  });\n});\n","numLines":199,"startLine":1,"totalLines":199}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_610e181b1f6648e891e49c60","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{jest} from '@jest/globals';\nimport {WebSocket} from 'ws';\nimport {createMessageHandler} from './messageHandler.js';\nimport {createChatOrchestrator, TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {ChatOrchestrator} from '../../orchestration/chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport {ToolRegistry} from '../../orchestration/tools/registry.js';\nimport {PromptBuilder} from '../../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\nimport type {AIProvider, MessageChunk, ToolCall} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport {AIError} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ChatSession, SessionEntry} from '../../types/session.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\nimport {PerSessionLock} from '../../shared/perSessionLock.js';\nimport {deferred} from '../wsTestSupport.js';\n\n// The frames, in order, are the contract - above all for suppression, which retracts.\n\n// One line per frame; entries carry generated timestamps no assertion should read.\nconst wire = (sent: OutgoingMessage[]): string[] =>\n  sent.map(frame => {\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_upsert') {\n      const content = 'content' in frame.entry ? frame.entry.content : '';\n      return `upsert ${frame.index} ${frame.entry.role} ${JSON.stringify(content)}`;\n    }\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_delta') return `delta ${frame.index} ${JSON.stringify(frame.delta)}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_commit') return `commit ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'entry_skip') return `skip ${frame.index}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'error') return `error ${frame.code}`;\n    if (frame.type === 'pong') return `pong ${frame.timestamp}`;\n    return frame.type;\n  });\n\nconst text = (value: string): MessageChunk => ({type: 'text', text: value});\nconst STOP: MessageChunk = {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\nconst SUPPRESS = {type: 'suppress_output'} as unknown as MessageChunk;\n\ninterface StreamScript {\n  failWith?: Error;\n  pauseAfter?: {chunks: number; until: Promise<void>};\n}\n\nconst harness = (chunks: MessageChunk[], {failWith, pauseAfter}: StreamScript = {}) => {\n  const sent: OutgoingMessage[] = [];\n  const ws = {send: (raw: string) => sent.push(JSON.parse(raw) as OutgoingMessage)} as unknown as WebSocket;\n\n  const stream = async function* (): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n    for (const [position, chunk] of chunks.entries()) {\n      if (pauseAfter && position === pauseAfter.chunks) await pauseAfter.until;\n      yield chunk;\n    }\n    if (failWith) throw failWith;\n  };\n\n  const processMessageStream = jest.fn(stream);\n  const orchestrator = {processMessageStream} as unknown as ChatOrchestrator;\n  const session: ChatSession = {sessionId: 's1', userId: 'u1', entries: []};\n\n  const handle = createMessageHandler(orchestrator);\n\n  return {\n    session,\n    processMessageStream,\n    sent,\n    frames: () => wire(sent),\n    send: (raw: unknown = {type: 'user_message', content: 'hello'}, signal?: AbortSignal) =>\n      handle(ws, session, raw, signal),\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('the websocket message handler', () => {\n  describe('dispatch', () => {\n    it('rejects an unparseable message and never starts a stream', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'nonsense'});\n\n      const {calls} = h.processMessageStream.mock;\n\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), streams: calls.length}).toEqual({frames: ['error INVALID_MESSAGE'], streams: 0});\n    });\n\n    it('answers a ping with the timestamp it was given', async () => {\n      const h = harness([]);\n\n      await h.send({type: 'ping', timestamp: 1234});\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['pong 1234']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('a plain assistant reply', () => {\n    it('sends the user entry, then the assistant entry, its delta, its commit and stream_end', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"hi there\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('leaves the committed assistant entry in the session, no longer streaming', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('hi there'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const {entries} = h.session;\n\n      expect(entries[1]).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hi there', isStreaming: false});\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('thinking segments', () => {\n    it('commits the thinking entry before the assistant entry opens', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>pondering</thinking>answer'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"pondering\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 2 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 2 \"answer\"',\n        'commit 2',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('commits the thinking entry when text resumes, not when a tool entry appears', async () => {\n      const h = harness([\n        text('<thinking>I should look up the weather for Berlin.</thinking>'),\n        {type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'get_weather', input: {location: 'Berlin'}}} as MessageChunk,\n        text('Berlin currently has '),\n        text('a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.'),\n        STOP,\n      ]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 thinking \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"I should look up the weather for Berlin.\"',\n        'upsert 2 tool \"\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 3 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 3 \"Berlin currently has \"',\n        'delta 3 \"a temperature of 18 degrees Celsius with clear skies.\"',\n        'commit 3',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('tool chunks', () => {\n    it('sends a tool entry for a tool call', async () => {\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_use', toolCall: {id: 'c1', name: 'lookup', input: {q: 1}}}, STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'upsert 1 tool \"\"', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n\n    it('forwards a tool result to the client untouched', async () => {\n      const forwarded = {type: 'entry_commit', index: 41} as OutgoingMessage;\n      const h = harness([{type: 'tool_result', clientMessages: [forwarded]} as MessageChunk, STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'commit 41', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe('suppression', () => {\n    it('blanks an assistant entry that was already sent', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('leaked'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual([\n        'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'delta 1 \"leaked\"',\n        'commit 1',\n        'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n        'stream_end',\n      ]);\n    });\n\n    it('never blanks a thinking entry, only assistant ones', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>private</thinking>said'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames().filter(frame => frame.startsWith('upsert 1'))).toEqual(['upsert 1 thinking \"\"']);\n    });\n\n    it('skips rather than upserts a segment opened after suppression', async () => {\n      const h = harness([SUPPRESS, text('hidden'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'skip 1', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n\n    it('still records a suppressed reply in the session, so history keeps it', async () => {\n      const h = harness([SUPPRESS, text('hidden'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const {entries} = h.session;\n\n      expect(entries[1]).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hidden', isStreaming: false});\n    });\n\n    it('does not resurrect an entry the client only ever saw skipped', async () => {\n      const h = harness([SUPPRESS, text('hidden'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames()).toEqual(['upsert 0 user \"hello\"', 'skip 1', 'stream_end']);\n    });\n\n    it('blanks each sent entry once, so a second suppression repeats nothing', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('leaked'), STOP, SUPPRESS, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      expect(h.frames().filter(frame => frame === 'upsert 1 assistant \"\"')).toHaveLength(2);\n    });\n\n    it('marks a sent assistant entry it blanked as suppressed in the session, keeping its text', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('leaked'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const [, answer] = h.session.entries;\n      expect(answer).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'leaked', suppressed: true});\n    });\n\n    it('marks a segment opened after suppression as suppressed in the session', async () => {\n      const h = harness([SUPPRESS, text('hidden'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const [, answer] = h.session.entries;\n      expect(answer).toMatchObject({role: 'assistant', content: 'hidden', suppressed: true});\n    });\n\n    it('leaves a thinking entry the client kept seeing unmarked, and marks the blanked answer', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>private</thinking>said'), STOP, SUPPRESS]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const [, thinking, answer] = h.session.entries;\n      expect({thinking: 'suppressed' in thinking, answer}).toMatchObject({\n        thinking: false,\n        answer: {role: 'assistant', content: 'said', suppressed: true},\n      });\n    });\n\n    it('commits and retracts an answer still open when suppression begins, and skips what follows as a new entry', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('before'), SUPPRESS, text(' after'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const [, answer, after] = h.session.entries;\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), answer, after}).toMatchObject({\n        frames: [\n          'upsert 0 user \"hello\"',\n          'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n          'delta 1 \"before\"',\n          'commit 1',\n          'upsert 1 assistant \"\"',\n          'skip 2',\n          'stream_end',\n        ],\n        answer: {role: 'assistant', content: 'before', isStreaming: false, suppressed: true},\n        after: {role: 'assistant', content: ' after', suppressed: true},\n      });\n    });\n\n    it('commits a thought still open when suppression begins as the client saw it, and skips what follows', async () => {\n      const h = harness([text('<thinking>early'), SUPPRESS, text(' later</thinking>'), STOP]);\n\n      await h.send();\n\n      const [, thought, after] = h.session.entries;\n      expect({frames: h.frames(), thought, marked: 'suppressed' in thought, after}).toMatchObject({\n        frames: [\n [];\n45\t\n46\t  const deps = {\n47\t    wsAuth: options.wsAuth,\n48\t    sessionStore: options.sessionStore,\n49\t    handleMessage,\n50\t    basePath,\n51\t    onConnect: options.onConnect,\n52\t    onDisconnect: options.onDisconnect,\n53\t    resume: options.resume,\n54\t  };\n55\t\n56\t  const handleUpgrade = createUpgradeHandler(wss, deps);\n57\t  const handleConnection = createConnectionHandler(deps, examplePrompts);\n58\t\n59\t  const server = http.createServer(options.app);\n60\t\n61\t  server.on('upgrade', (request, socket, head) => {\n62\t    handleUpgrade(request, socket, head);\n63\t  });\n64\t\n65\t  wss.on('connection', ws => {\n66\t    handleConnection(ws as ExtWebSocket);\n67\t  });\n68\t\n69\t  const heartbeatMs = options.heartbeatIntervalMs ?? 30_000;\n70\t\n71\t  const heartbeatInterval = setInterval(() => {\n72\t    wss.clients.forEach(ws => {\n73\t      const extWs = ws as ExtWebSocket;\n74\t      if (!extWs.isAlive) {\n75\t        extWs.terminate();\n76\t        return;\n77\t      }\n78\t      extWs.isAlive = false;\n79\t      extWs.ping();\n80\t    });\n81\t  }, heartbeatMs);\n82\t\n83\t  // The listening socket should hold the process open, not the heartbeat: an engine never started must not.\n84\t  heartbeatInterval.unref();\n85\t\n86\t  wss.on('close', () => clearInterval(heartbeatInterval));\n87\t\n88\t  return {\n89\t    server,\n90\t    wss,\n91\t    start: (port?: number) =>\n92\t      new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {\n93\t        // Refused before the handlers are touched: `listen` throws on a running server, and the swap below stripped its handler.\n94\t        if (server.listening) {\n95\t          reject(new Error('HAL Engine is already started'));\n96\t          return;\n97\t        }\n98\t\n99\t        // ?? not ||, so a configured port 0 means \"let the OS choose\" rather than 8086.\n100\t        const p = port ?? options.port ?? '/hal';\n\n  const wss = new WebSocketServer({\n    noServer: true,\n    handleProtocols: selectSubprotocol,\n  });\n\n  const handleMessage = createMessageHandler(options.orchestrator);\n  const examplePrompts = options.toolRegistry?.getExamplePrompts() ?? be open.\n  if (!resumed) join(session, ws);\n\n  if (state.closed) {\n    // Held first: a store that implements no evict still holds this session, and it carries the caller's credentials.\n    held.session = session;\n    await evictUnlessResumed(deps, sessionId, resumed);\n    endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n    ws.resume();\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (resumed) join(resumed, ws);\n  held.session = session;\n\n  log.info('ws', 'connected', {sessionId, userId: ws.userId});\n\n  const connected: ConnectedMessage = {\n    type: 'connected',\n    sessionId,\n    message: 'Connected to HAL Engine',\n    examplePrompts,\n    ...resumeFields(deps.resume, outcome),\n  };\n  // A socket that died between the check above and this frame must not leave the session it was created for behind.\n  try {\n    ws.send(JSON.stringify(connected));\n    if (resumed) replayEntries(ws, resumed);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'connected frame failed', {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n    await evictUnlessResumed(deps, sessionId, resumed);\n    endSession(deps, sessionId, state, held);\n    ws.resume();\n    ws.close(1011, 'Connection setup failed');\n    return;\n  }\n\n  state.delivered = true;\n\n  // Deferred, not inline: a synchronous throw in the `connection` listener corrupts an already-upgraded socket.\n\n  // A microtask, not setImmediate: it drains before the loop delivers any inbound frame on this socket.\n  queueMicrotask(() =>\n    runHook('onConnect', sessionId, () => deps.onConnect?.(session, {resumed: resumed !== undefined}))\n  );\n\n  ws.on('message', (frame: Buffer | string) => {\n    const parsed = parseWsData(frame);\n    if (parsed === null) {\n      sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.INVALID_FORMAT, 'Invalid JSON');\n      return;\n    }\n    log.info('ws', 'message received', {sessionId, type: (parsed as Record<string, unknown>).type as string});\n    deps.handleMessage(ws, session, parsed, connection.signal);\n  });\n\n  ws.resume();\n}\n\n// Joined as the newest socket on the session, which carries this upgrade's credentials from here on.\nfunction join(session: ChatSession, ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n  openSockets.set(session, [...(openSockets.get(session) ?? []), ws]);\n  session.authHeaders = ws.authHeaders;\n}\n\n// `undefined` rather than a throw: one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process.\nasync function createSession(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  ws: ExtWebSocket\n): Promise<ChatSession | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await deps.sessionStore.create(sessionId, ws.userId, {\n      authHeaders: ws.authHeaders,\n      workspaceId: ws.workspaceId,\n    });\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'session create failed', {userId: ws.userId, error: messageOf(error)});\n    sendError(ws, ErrorCodes.SERVER_ERROR, 'Could not start a session');\n    return undefined;\n  }\n}\n\n// The close path erases nothing: the conversation outlives its socket, and `onDisconnect` is the consumer's seam.\nfunction endSession(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  state: {notified: boolean; delivered: boolean},\n  held: {session?: ChatSession; socket: ExtWebSocket}\n): void {\n  if (state.notified) return;\n  state.notified = true;\n\n  if (held.session) leave(held.session, held.socket);\n\n  // Only for a session the consumer was actually handed: onDisconnect is the other half of onConnect, not of a socket.\n  if (!state.delivered) return;\n\n  runHook('onDisconnect', sessionId, () => deps.onDisconnect?.(sessionId));\n}\n\n// The newest socket still open lends the session its credentials; with none left, nothing keeps them or a closed socket.\nfunction leave(session: ChatSession, ws: ExtWebSocket): void {\n  const open = openSockets.get(session) ?? [];\n  if (!open.includes(ws)) return;\n  const remaining = open.filter(socket => socket !== ws);\n  const newest = remaining.at(-1);\n  if (newest === undefined) {\n    openSockets.delete(session);\n    session.authHeaders = undefined;\n    return;\n  }\n  openSockets.set(session, remaining);\n  session.authHeaders = newest.authHeaders;\n}\n\n// Never a resumed session: evict erases, and a resumed session holds the conversation being rejoined.\nasync function evictUnlessResumed(\n  deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps,\n  sessionId: string,\n  resumed: ChatSession | undefined\n): Promise<void> {\n  if (!resumed) await evictSession(deps, sessionId);\n}\n\n// Only for a session no client ever received: it has no entries and nothing to migrate.\nasync function evictSession(deps: ConnectionHandlerDeps, sessionId: string): Promise<void> {\n  try {\n    await deps.sessionStore.evict?.(sessionId);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.error('ws', 'session evict failed', {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n  }\n}\n\n// Consumer hooks are fire-and-forget: the engine never awaits one and never lets one take the connection down.\nfunction runHook(name: string, sessionId: string, call: () => void | Promise<void>): void {\n  try {\n    // Promise.resolve also absorbs a thenable from another realm, where `instanceof Promise` is false.\n    void Promise.resolve(call()).catch((error: unknown) => logHookFailure(name, sessionId, error));\n  } catch (error) {\n    logHookFailure(name, sessionId, error);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction logHookFailure(name: string, sessionId: string, error: unknown): void {\n  log.error('ws', `${name} hook failed`, {sessionId, error: messageOf(error)});\n}\n\nfunction messageOf(error: unknown): string {\n  if (typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'message' in error) return String(error.message);\n  return String(error);\n}\n","numLines":302,"startLine":1,"totalLines":302}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_60a2022cdcbd4ee6a14c43c4","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

The ticket says \"no user content\" in the log — sessionId and userId are identifiers, fine (the acceptance test requires userId in fields explicitly).\n\nError frame message: \"Failed to list conversations\" — carries no store detail. Good.\n\n`toSummaryFrame`:\n\n```ts\nconst toSummaryFrame = (summary: SessionSummary): SessionSummaryFrame => ({\n  sessionId: summary.sessionId,\n  createdAt: new Date(summary.createdAt).toISOString(),\n  updatedAt: new Date(summary.updatedAt).toISOString(),\n  entryCount: summary.entryCount,\n});\n```\n\nHmm — `new Date(dateObj)` works. For a Date, `.toISOString()` directly is the typed path. `SessionSummary` declares Date. But stores coming through JSON... The type says Date; minimal green: `summary.createdAt.toISOString()`. Robustness vs green. The dod says \"serialising `Date` fields to ISO strings\". I'll use `new Date(...)` — no wait, keep it typed and simple: `.toISOString()`. Hmm, but what if a store returns string dates (a JSON-backed store)? Type says Date; TS would flag it, not my problem this round. Actually `new Date(summary.createdAt as Date)`... no. Keep `.toISOString()` — simplest typed implementation. Hmm, but honestly `new Date(x).toISOString()` handles Date | string | number with no cast and is strictly more tolerant; it costs nothing. I'll go with `new Date(...)` form? Let me think about which reads better in this codebase... There's likely an existing ISO helper somewhere. And callers with 1 arg keep working (optional param).\n\n8. Jest has no dry-run, so the list command executes the suite\n    once with --json and derives every name from the report; it deliberately\n    tolerates a red suite, since listing must not depend on the tests passing.\n    The run command selects one test with --runTestsByPath plus an anchored,\n    regex-escaped -t, and treats a selector that matches nothing as a failure\n    rather than a green run of an empty suite. Neither command builds first:\n    no test here reads dist/.\n  list: node scripts/lore-list-tests.mjs\n  run: node scripts/lore-run-test.mjs \"{selector}\"\n  coverage_format: lcov\nsrc/transport/createApp.ts:39:      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\nsrc/transport/routes/chats.ts:53:    const createdAt = new Date().toISOString();\nsrc/transport/routes/chats.ts:89:      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\nsrc/transport/routes/chats.ts:111:        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\nsrc/shared/logger.ts:25:    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\nsrc/orchestration/entryFactories.ts:4:  return {role: 'user', content, timestamp: new Date().toISOString()};\nsrc/orchestration/entryFactories.ts:8:  return {role: 'assistant', content: '', timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), isStreaming: true};\nsrc/orchestration/entryFactories.ts:16:  return {role: 'tool', toolName, toolInput, timestamp: new Date().toISOString()};\n# Conversation List\n\n| Field  | Value                 |\n| ------ | --------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#143 |\n| Status | Shipped               |\n\nResume gets a client back into one conversation: the id it names, or the user's most recently active one. Neither tells it which conversations exist, and every other member of `SessionStore` answers about a session the caller can already name, so a consumer wanting to offer a conversation list had to query the collection behind the engine's back, against a document shape and a key the engine owns. `listFor` answers the list instead, as summaries rather than sessions. **GDPR.** A summary is personal data — that a user held a conversation, and when — so it carries no conversation content, it is filtered to one user by the query rather than in application code afterwards, and the retention bound stays the consumer's, through the store's `maxAgeMs` and erasure methods and re-cinq/HALEngine#41.\n\n## The summary\n\n- A summary is `sessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` and `entryCount`, and nothing else: neither the conversation's entries nor its credentials, so a list can never hand over either, even for a session created with credentials ([validated by: carries only its four fields, so a list can never hand over a conversation or a credential](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L22)).\n- `listFor` is optional, like `latestFor` and `lookup` before it: a store written against the five original members still satisfies the interface, and both shipped stores implement it ([validated by: leaves a store with only the five original members satisfying the interface beside both shipped ones](../../src/infrastructure/stores/sessionStoreListSignature.test.ts#L11)).\n\n## The order a list answers in\n\n- Summaries come back most recent activity first ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The first summary is the session `latestFor` returns, because both read the same activity ([validated by: answers newest activity first, headed by the very session latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L27)).\n- The order is total rather than merely sorted: two conversations last active in the same millisecond are ordered by session id, the larger first, which is what lets a page resume without dropping one of them ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- In `InMemorySessionStore` that tie-break is the list's alone: `latestFor` breaks the same tie by creation order, so for two tied conversations the head of the list and the session a resume rejoins can differ ([validated by: breaks a tie on activity by session id, where latestFor takes the session created later](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L42)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers in order of `updatedAt`, which each `save` moves forward, and its first summary is the session its own `latestFor` returns ([validated by: answers the user's conversations newest saved first, headed by the one latestFor returns](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L31)).\n- It breaks a tie by `_id` in both members, so there the head of the list is the session a resume rejoins even when every conversation shares an `updatedAt` ([validated by: heads the list with the session latestFor returns even when every conversation shares an updatedAt](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L161)).\n\n## What a summary reports\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` reports the moment `create` was called, the newest entry time as the activity, and the conversation's entry count ([validated by: reports a creation time, the newest activity and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L53)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reports the document's `createdAt`, the `updatedAt` its last save wrote, and the counter written beside the entries ([validated by: reports the creation time, the last save and the entry count of each conversation](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L49)).\n- That counter is what a save writes, so a list never reads a conversation to count one ([validated by: counts a conversation from the field a save writes beside the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L95)).\n- A document written before the counter existed reads as a conversation of no entries rather than failing the list, which is what the backlog documented in `docs/session-stores.md` is for ([validated by: reads a conversation saved before the counter existed as one of no entries, rather than failing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L79)).\n\n## Whose conversations\n\n- A list holds only the asking user's conversations: another user's never appear, and a user with none gets an empty list ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `InMemorySessionStore` omits a conversation that has aged out, as `latestFor` does ([validated by: omits a conversation that aged out and another user's, and answers nothing for a user with none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L65)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` filters on the user in the database, sorts on `{updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` — the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1}` index `latestFor` already needs serves its leading keys — and asks for a projection that leaves the entries behind ([validated by: asks the database to filter on the user, sort on the index with the id behind it, and never for the entries](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L108)).\n- It answers from that projection alone, so a collection that never returns an entry still lists conversations — the conversation does not leave the database to be listed ([validated by: answers from a projection alone, so a collection that never returns entries still lists conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L181)).\n\n## Paging\n\n- `limit` takes that many of the newest, and `before` resumes after a row, so a client pages by passing back the last summary it saw — `SessionCursor` is `updatedAt` and `sessionId`, which a `SessionSummary` already satisfies ([validated by: pages down the same order: a limit takes the newest, and before takes what is older than it](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L78)).\n- Paging walks every conversation exactly once even when all of them share an activity time, because the cursor carries the session id the order breaks ties on: a tie cannot fall between two pages and be skipped ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on activity rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L141)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` pages the same way ([validated by: pages with before and a limit, down the same newest-first order](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L62)).\n- It walks a tie exactly once too, through the same cursor ([validated by: keeps a conversation tied on updatedAt rather than dropping it across a page boundary](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L127)).\n- A list is at most 200 summaries however many are asked for, and 50 when none is asked for, so no caller can ask for an unbounded page ([validated by: answers at most two hundred conversations however many are asked for, and fifty when none is](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L94)).\n- That limit bounds the rows answered, not the rows the database reads to answer them: on `MongoSessionStore` the work is bounded by the `{userId: 1, updatedAt: -1, _id: -1}` index `docs/session-stores.md` prescribes, and under the two-key form Mongo sorts the user's whole history before applying the limit ([validated by: needs the three-key index to answer without sorting the whole history, which the two-key form does not](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L192)).\n- A fractional limit is floored rather than refused, since a slip in a limit is not a reason to deny a user their history ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- A negative limit, and one that is not a usable number, are read as no limit given at all rather than as a limit of none: handing a user an empty history for a typo is the worse reading ([validated by: floors a fractional limit, and reads a negative or unusable one as none given rather than as nothing](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L104)).\n- Only a limit of exactly `0` answers no conversations ([validated by: answers nothing only for a limit of exactly none](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L116)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` answers a limit of `0` without querying, because MongoDB reads `limit: 0` as no limit at all and would otherwise answer with every conversation the filter matches ([validated by: answers a limit of none without asking the database, which reads a limit of zero as no limit at all](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L143)).\n\n## The two shipped stores answer one order\n\n- `InMemorySessionStore` and `MongoSessionStore` list the same conversations in the same order, so a consumer swapping one for the other sees the same conversation list ([validated by: answer the same order for conversations whose activity differs](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L43)).\n- They break a tie on activity the same way, by session id ([validated by: break a tie on activity the same way, by session id](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L52)).\n- They page identically through the documented call, `listFor(userId, {limit, before: rows.at(-1)})`, a page at a time until a page comes back empty ([validated by: page the same way through the documented call, two rows at a time from the last row seen](../../src/infrastructure/stores/storeListAgreement.test.ts#L61)).\n\n## A cursor the caller can actually hold\n\n- A cursor's `updatedAt` may be a `Date`, an ISO string or an epoch number, so a summary that went through JSON on its way to a client and back still pages ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n- `MongoSessionStore` reads such a cursor as a date before it queries, since a string compares against no stored BSON date and would quietly match none of them ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, where a string would have matched no stored date](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L150)).\n- A cursor carrying no usable moment is refused with an error naming it, rather than read as no cursor at all, which would answer the first page again and repeat rows a client has already shown ([validated by: pages on a cursor that has been through JSON, and refuses one carrying no usable moment](../../src/infrastructure/stores/inMemoryConversationList.test.ts#L123)).\n\n## A collection that cannot list\n\n- `find` is optional on `CollectionLike`, so an adapter written before conversation lists existed still satisfies the port ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n- A store built on a collection without it refuses to list, rather than reporting that the user has no conversations ([validated by: refuses to list on a collection that implements no find, rather than reporting no conversations](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L175)).\n\n## When the store cannot answer\n\n- A store whose collection fails rejects rather than answering a partial or empty list: what to show a user who may have conversations is the caller's decision, and an empty history is not a safe guess ([validated by: rejects rather than answering a partial list when the collection fails](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoConversationList.test.ts#L225)).\n\n## Over the WebSocket protocol\n\n- A client sends `{type: 'list_sessions', limit?, before?}` and receives `{type: 'session_list', sessions}` for the socket's authenticated user, with `createdAt` and `updatedAt` serialised as ISO-8601 strings and any client-supplied `userId` ignored ([validated by: answers list_sessions for the authenticated user with ISO dates, forwarding limit and before while ignoring any client userId](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L93)).\n- A store without `listFor` answers `{type: 'session_list', sessions: []}`, and a throwing `listFor` logs an error on the `ws` category and answers `{type: 'error', code: 'SERVER_ERROR'}` ([validated by: answers an empty session_list when the store has no listFor, and SERVER_ERROR with a ws error log when listFor throws](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L134)).\n- The validator accepts an optional non-negative integer `limit` and an optional `before` cursor whose `sessionId` is 1–128 characters and whose `updatedAt` parses as a valid timestamp, rejecting any other `list_sessions` payload with `INVALID_MESSAGE` without calling `listFor` ([validated by: accepts a bare list_sessions frame and rejects a malformed limit or before with INVALID_MESSAGE without calling listFor](../../src/transport/conversationList.acceptance.test.ts#L163), [validated by: accepts list_sessions with an optional limit and before cursor, and names the field a malformed frame fails on](../../src/transport/ws/validation.test.ts#L25)).","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f773dd4f-97e5-4bea-b135-1a2d9a59db99","uuid":"53dc027f-6eb2-4340-b9bf-1797cdb77e65","timestamp":"2026-11-04T00:39:38.558Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#
